name: Point Nepean National Park
signature: The Peninsula's most historically layered walk — through Fort Nepean's military ruins to the very tip of the land, with ocean on both sides
editorNote:
Point Nepean National Park occupies the narrow tip of the Peninsula and contains one of the most extraordinary walks in coastal Victoria. The track passes through the ruins of Fort Nepean — a fortification that guarded Port Phillip Heads from the 1880s through World War II and fired the first Allied shot of both World Wars — before arriving at the very tip of the land, where Port Phillip Bay meets Bass Strait in a tidal rush through the Heads.

The walk is 8km return from the visitor centre to the fort, with a bus option for those who prefer a shorter day. Bikes are also permitted. The coastal scenery — ocean on one side, bay on the other, native scrub and historic fortifications throughout — is unlike anything else on the Peninsula.

Book the entry pass online. Arrive early in summer. Bring water — there are no facilities at the tip.
whyWeGo: History, coastal drama, and the literal end of the Peninsula — Point Nepean is unlike anything else on the Mornington.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk the full 8km to the fort. The tidal rush through the Heads at the tip is worth every step.
